name: @shepherd/ext-editor
description: shepherd.editor — the files of a task's worktrees, editable, and what you changed in them.
//exports: The split every extension makes: main imports ./manifest to register, the utility process imports the root (which pulls in `activate`), and ./ui is the half the renderer mounts.
//pierre: The same buy `github` made, for the same two panels — and the reason this extension needs no editor of its own. `@pierre/trees` is the file list; `@pierre/diffs` is BOTH halves of the right-hand panel, because it ships a real editor (`/edit`, and `<File edit>`) as well as the diff renderer. One vendor means the file and its diff are the same surface under the same registered theme. A vendor dependency an extension owns privately: the boundary lint is about which SHEPHERD packages an extension may reach.
//dependencies: @shepherd/ext-tasks and @shepherd/ext-scratch are TYPE-ONLY — `import type` and nothing else. The runtime relationship is the command id plus the manifest's `dependencies` entry, which is the gate the host can review; a value import would route around it. See extensions/README.md.
//shepherd: The manifest, as an extension declares it. `src/manifest.ts` is the typed copy the host loads, and `manifest.test.ts` asserts the two are identical.
//ui: The UI half, imported ONLY by the renderer (boundaries.js). A separate subpath because it is a separate PROCESS: `.` is the service half and runs in a utility process with no DOM.
